definition: why a lapsed habit is gated at a higher safety level than the same habit running

settled:
The difficulty my gate compares against belongs to the state of an activity rather than to the activity.

Restarting a lapsed habit from cold is scored a rung or more higher than keeping the same habit going while it is live.

So a thing can be maintainable the whole time it is running, lapse for some unrelated reason, and then be no option at all. Its steady cost did not rise. The gate is now pricing the restart, and my level no longer clears that.

Through any stretch below the restart line I am gated out of a thing that maintaining would have been fine.

What this tells me to do is protect a live habit from lapsing in the first place, and to expect getting back in to wait for a higher level than the thing itself looks like it needs.

title: Restarting A Habit Costs More Than Keeping It
